   Introduction to MASTERFILE
   & Changes  by Brian Cavers
   --------------------------
MASTERFILE was published in the
early days of the Spectrum but I
don't know of any other Spectrum
all-purpose, record-keeping pro-
gram to beat it! The publishers,
Campbell Systems, have now made
it public domain so it can be
freely copied.

MASTERFILE enables you to keep
records of almost any type, show
them sorted in any order either
on screen or printed, either the
complete file or a selected part
of it and search  the file for a
particular item or items, e.g.,
every London address from a name
and address list!


You can add, modify or remove a
record and the whole file can be
saved to tape or disc for later
retrieval or update.

The original was for 48K use and
became Version 09 very early on.
This worked only with ZX-type
printers but Campbell later put
out "MFPRINT" which modifies the
main MASTERFILE to use full-size
printers.

I have seen a Version 10 but I
think it was someone's modified
version and not an "official"
version number. There is also a
128K version for the +3 with an
increased storage capacity and
extra features which will be in
a later (next?) issue on the +3
OUTLET disc only.

In addition, I have made further
improvements to the original 48K
Version 9 which I have named 9B.
This now includes a choice of an
extra, thicker, screen character
set; the ability to "ADD" or
"MERGE" separate files; no need
for a "pre-loader" to clear down
RAMTOP; the extra MFPRINT of
course; as well as lots of extra
little goodies I shall describe
later.

The foregoing does use a little
more of the precious memory even
though I have improved memory-
saving on the BASIC that already
existed so I have also created a
"bare-minimum" version that is
the original Version 09 with the
BASIC reduced even more.


I recommend you use Version 9B.
If a file becomes too large you
can either split it into two or,
if preferred, load it into the
cut-down version and add more to
it but note that it will not
then load into the full version.

Our OUTLET index: OUTDEX which
became full up last December, is
now to be relaunched each month
as a MASTERFILE file. This was
the main reason for my writing a
"MERGE" routine so that you can
add each month's new index data
to your main OUTDEX file until
it is full, at which point just
start a "Volume 2". An advantage
of MASTERFILE is that it does
not matter which order you add
these files as they are shown in
the right order.

The full original OUTDEX (Issues
1 to 63) has been converted to
MASTERFILE format and is in this
issue as "OUTDEX1.63". Just load
it in MASTERFILE.

All later months' data up to
last month is in a separate file
"OUTDX64.74". Future OUTDEX data
will usually be one month behind
with a filename, eg.,"OUTDEX.75"
so just keep adding (merging)
them into "OUTDX64.74"and resave
as eg, "OUTDEX64.75" until full!

We've TWO parts of instructions
so for a fast look at MASTERFILE
press N (twice!) and follow the
menus to load and display OUTDEX
data else read on or print the
following more detailed info...

When MASTERFILE was declared in
the public domain I appealed for
readers to send in copies so an
assessment of the different ver-
sions could be made etc. So many
readers kindly helped out that I
am confident we have everything
and all instructions.

There were just too many people
to credit everyone here but each
should have received an individ-
ual acknowledgement on return of
their disc. THANKS AGAIN TO ALL!

We have received various bits of
instructions and programs and it
is possible some parts have been
published in the SDC Newsletters
for which we give credit. I have
modified and added also!


As saved in OUTLET, MASTERFILE
includes our usual OUTLET 'link'
BASIC and title page. All this
superfluous programming erases
itself automatically when you
use the RUN option. DO NOT USE
THE MASTERFILE 'SAVE PROGRAM'
OPTION TO RESAVE MASTERFILE ON
YOUR OUTLET DISC AS "MFILE" OR
IT WILL NO LONGER LINK TO OUTLET
(in fact it is always best to
keep any original program as a
back up - completely unchanged
in case of disaster!).

In addition, take care when you
save a file separately from the
main program that you don't use
the same name as your program,
e.g., "MFILE" or it will over-
write the program if it is on
the same disc!        - Brian

        GLOSSARY OF TERMS
        -----------------
ADD: Merge another file into the
current file from disc/tape - OR
insert a new RECORD in the file.

ARGUMENT: In a SEARCH, something
with which RECORDS are compared.

AUTO-PROMPT:Where new data ITEMS
are solicited automatically.

BACK OUT: Change one's mind.

COMMAND MODE: In BASIC.

DATA NAME: Fuller name of DATA
REFERENCE or FIELD.

DATA REFERENCE: Letter A-Z by
which FIELDS are identified.


DISPLAY MODE: Where SELECTED
RECORDS are viewed in a REPORT.

EDIT MODE: Where REPORT formats
are created or altered.

EMPTY FILE:One devoid of RECORDS
DATA NAMES or REPORT FORMATS.

FIELD: Part of record,identified
by its DATA REFERENCE,that holds
one ITEM of data.

FILE:Whole collection of RECORDS
(subdivided into ITEMS)and their
associated REPORT FORMATS etc.

GENERAL:Global Report attributes

INVERT: Reverse SELECTED status
of all RECORDS - thus UNSELECTED
become SELECTEd and vice versa.

ITEM:Data,1-128 characters long,
a subsection of a RECORD. One
ITEM of data fits into one FIELD
of the file identified by its
DATA REFERENCE and DATA NAME.

LITERAL TEXT: Fixed text, e.g.,
a heading in a REPORT.

MAIN MENU: The MENU offered when
the program is first run (=MM).

MENU: List of key options.

MICRO-PRINT:Screen text shown at
42 or 51 characters a line.

MM: MAIN MENU.

NULL TEXT: Text displayed in a
REPORT in the absence of an ITEM


PAD:Fill out data with spaces in
a REPORT.

PROMPT: Instruction to the user,
or small MENU.

PURGE:Erase all SELECTED RECORDS

RAM: Random Access Memory avail-
able for operating the program

RECORD:Set of upto 26 ITEMS,each
with a different DATA REFERENCE.

REPORT:List of SELECTED RECORDS.

REPORT ELEMENT:Part of a REPORT,
e.g., heading, box, data spec.

REPORT REFERENCE: Character 0-9
or A-Z identifying a REPORT.


RESET: Clear SELECTED status of
all RECORDS, ie, deselect all.

SEARCH MODE: Where RECORDS are
SELECTED or otherwise by compar-
ing with an ARGUMENT.

SELECTED: Eligible for display
in a REPORT.

SEQUENCE:Where RECORDS are shown
in order of a chosen FIELD.

UPDATE MODE: Where a RECORD can
be altered.

USER BASIC: BASIC which you can
supply for special processing.

VLC: Vertical Line Character=New
line.see WORDPROCESSING(Page 55)


     MASTERFILE INSTRUCTIONS
     -----------------------

     If any of the terms used
     are unfamiliar, refer to
     the  preceding  glossary
     that starts  on Page 09.

            OVERVIEW
            --------

MASTERFILE is a filing and re-
trieval system for use with any
Spectrum. It is almost entirely
machine-coded for compactness
and speed and offers about 30K
of data per file.The program can
be saved and loaded with a file
"on board" for immediate access
or files can be saved and loaded
independently (tape or disc).


Because MASTERFILE display form-
ats are user-defined, the range
of applications is enormous both
for domestic use and business.
Address lists,library catalogues
personnel files, stock inventor-
ies, school exam results, family
trees - all these are easily
handled by MASTERFILE. Some of
the main features are:

* Menu-driven, dynamic,variable-
  length file.

* User-defined data names and
  report formats.

* File search by any number of
  criteria.

* Sequence order by any field.


* Display 1-22 records a screen.

* Micro-print feature for up to
  51 characters per line.

* Print to any printer including
  the old ZX-types.

* Total and average calculations
  for fields containing values.

* Optional User BASIC where the
  file data is passed to BASIC
  in sequence so the user can
  perform any other calculations
  or modification of the data.

* Update,copy and erase records.

* Save or load files or program.

* Speed of operation.

    MASTERFILE FILE STRUCTURE
    -------------------------
A file is an organised collect-
ion of data (subdivided into
records further subdivided into
data items) which is stored on
cassette or disc and which can
be loaded into RAM for enquiry
or update purposes.

It may be simple as a telephone
list or complex like a personnel
data file but, in every case, a
file is made up of records, each
of which is usually related to a
particular identifying item e.g.
a person, recipe or part-number.

Each record is in turn made up
of up to 26 different items of
data e.g., name, address, stock
level, telephone number.

Data items are all treated by
MASTERFILE as being of variable
length (so no memory is wasted)
up to 128 characters in length.

There is no rigid record struct-
ure and items can be stored in
any order within a record as
they may always be displayed or
printed in the order you define.
Each data item in a record is in
an individual field identified
by its unique data reference
letter. A record can have many
DIFFERENT fields but cannot have
the SAME one more than once (eg,
if you wanted both home AND work
phone numbers you must have two
different fields or put them in
together and treat as one item.
All data is stored in character
format (as text or digits).

One of the many advantages of a
computer file over a card index
system is that you can sort it
into any order. MASTERFILE does
not actually sort your file into
order (as stored) but instead
DISPLAYS it in any chosen sorted
order (a much faster method).You
can thus have different logical
views of the same data in diff-
erent sequences as well as your
original date-entered order.

Further, you can be selective
about which items are required
in a report and choose the
display style. You may compose a
report format for each view of
the file you need. Once these
formats are built,they are saved
automatically as part of a file.

While items are referred to with
a single reference letter which
denotes its field,you can assoc-
iate a full word or phrase with
each such reference. MASTERFILE
will display these whenever you
use data references especially
in AUTO-PROMPT (p.58). We call
them "DATA NAMES" and these are
also stored automatically as
part of your file.


         PLANNING A FILE
         ---------------
We recommend you work through
the section entitled EXERCISE on
Page 3 of the next part of these
instructions before starting
your own file. After that, we
suggest the following approach..

The most important task is to
decide what data is to go into
each record. Allocate a letter
A-Z to each kind of data you
wish to store. Try to estimate
an average record size by adding
together what you think will be
the usual number of characters
in each item. Add 1 for each
reference letter (which is also
stored). Divide this into 30,000
to get the approximate maximum
number of records. Also allow a
few dozen bytes for EACH report
format which you will compose.
Is the answer enough? If not,can
you reduce anywhere?For example,
where the length of a particular
item of data is purely optional,
e.g., personal notes, you may
prefer to keep these brief and
thus get more records in a file.

Remember,any item can be present
or not in a record. For example,
if you define a field for an
item of data that is a phone
number, you don't need to use
that field in any particular
record -it can be empty.However,
you cannot have more than one
item of the SAME data reference
in one record. For example: you
couldn't enter TWO phone numbers
as SEPARATE ITEMS each with the
data reference "T" in one record
but you may put them both in
together as one item. This would
not waste space on those records
with only one phone number but
you must leave room on-screen in
case there were two. Otherwise,
define a separate field (data
reference) as say,"X" for "Xtra"
phone number!.

The next step is to allocate a
name or description for each
data reference. For example, if
you have chosen the data refer-
ence letter "T" for a telephone
number field then you might use
"TELEPHONE" as the data name.

This is optional however; you do
not need to give a full name at
all if you don't want to but it
is useful - and almost essential
if using AUTO-PROMPT (see p.3 of
the next part of these instruct-
ions).The method of allocating
this name is as described in
DATA NAMES (p.37) after creating
an EMPTY FILE (p.35).

Next, add just a few records,see
ADD A RECORD MODE (p.57).


Next comes the hard work where
you must design and specify the
way you want to view your file.
Remember that you can have many
different views, different
sequences, different formats and
different contents.


Start with a simple format - it
may be helpful to plan it on
paper first.Leave embellishments
such as lines and boxes until
last after you have "frozen" the
positions of your data and head-
ings. Give special attention to
the "interval" which affects the
spacing between the displayed
records - see EDIT MODE (p.38),
MICROPRINT (p.51) and WORDPROC-
ESSING (p.55).


     MENUS, PROMPTS, MODES
     ---------------------

MASTERFILE menus are yellow and
respond to upper-case or lower-
case keys impartially. When
MASTERFILE is loaded it presents
the Main Menu: MM. The MM screen
also displays the file name (up
to 10 characters) and the MASTER
FILE version number.

When a key corresponding to one
of the options is used, MASTER
FILE either takes the indicated
action, or immediately offers
another menu or prompt. A prompt
is a one-line instruction or
menu in the lower part of the
screen, and takes priority over
any other menu.


All the yellow menus and prompts
respond to just a single key but
where MASTERFILE needs a textual
response, the flashing L cursor
appears and you terminate your
response with the ENTER key.

MASTERFILE nearly always offers
a menu or prompt but there is
one exception: when in DISPLAY
mode the menu would obliterate
your display, so it is not
usually shown. But you can
overlay your display with the
menu by using the Q key - BUT
USE Q AGAIN to REMOVE the menu.

MASTERFILE operates in a variety
of modes - usually shown by a
blue heading EXCEPT in DISPLAY
mode where ALL lines 0-21 are
left to you.

DISPLAY mode will always show
"Report n" in red on line 22.
Important modes are described in
the glossary and some modes: MM,
SEARCH, DISPLAY - are accessible
by several menu routes.

It would be a little dangerous
to allow a single-key response
to erase data, so MASTERFILE
always asks for confirmation via
the "Y" key.Likewise, User BASIC
is potentially drastic, and
again requires Y to confirm. If
you see "Y to confirm" you can
back out with any key except Y.
Version 9B User BASIC exits to
an extra menu which includes a
further option for "User BASIC
processing" which, as provided,
simply STOPS.


       BASIC COMMAND MODE
       ------------------

With a few exceptions,MASTERFILE
runs under machine code control
and the BREAK key is ineffective
but if you need to modify the
Basic or add your own User Basic
then you must get into COMMAND
mode.

This can be done when MASTERFILE
offers a flashing L cursor, e.g.
press L at MM. If you then press
the CURSOR DOWN key, you get "H
STOP in INPUT". Alternatively,
select the User BASIC menu then
BREAK will work. You are now in
COMMAND mode and can list and
alter the BASIC.


To resume MASTERFILE processing,
enter "GO TO 1" which takes you
to the Main Menu again. GO TO 1
should also be used to recover
any accidental drop into COMMAND
mode.Do not CLEAR or RUN because
it will crash MASTERFILE and you
will lose any data not SAVEd.

         GETTING STARTED
         ---------------
MASTERFILE uses several linked
files...

     MFILE  main program
      MF.C  main code
SCRNEDIT.C  screen report editor
 MFPRINT.C  ext. printer overlay
  FORMSPEC  formats printer spec
   ANYNAME  your printer specs.
   ANYNAME  your data files

In addition there is the cutdown
version: MFILE.MIN and MFMIN.C.

You will normally load MFILE and
this loads the main code. It can
be used immediately without any
change but you will normally re-
save it as your working copy on
another disc using any name you
wish for the main program.

When a data file is in memory,
it will be saved with the main
program so you can name the main
program with a name relevant to
the file, e.g.,"BIRTHDAYS". When
you reload that copy of the pro-
gram all the data is immediately
available. Alternatively, save
the file on its own and load it
into the main program when you
need it..

        MAIN MENU OPTIONS
        -----------------
The main menu represents the top
logical level of processing and
offers functions which affect
the file as a whole. Some func-
tions are described more fully
elsewhere.

A Add a new record to the end of
  the file. A one-byte record is
  inserted and you can see the
  "Recs=" and "Sel=" counts inc-
  rement. See ADD A RECORD(p.57)

C Lists all report formats (WITH
  THE FIRST-ENTERED LITERAL TEXT
  HEADING) of each report which
  you can select to display the
  data in that report format.You
  can use ENTER to return to MM.


D Go directly to DISPLAY mode to
  view selected records using
  the last report format used or
  the first one created if not
  yet displayed. If there are no
  report formats yet, EDIT mode
  is entered.Several other menus
  offer a D option. See DISPLAY
  MODE (p.60).

E EDIT mode (p.38) to review or
  update screen report formats.

   OR...

  EXTENDED PRINTER options (p.47
  of Part 2) [the Main Menu will
  show the current E option].

L Load a file which has been
  saved via MM V,F etc. See LOAD
  AND SAVE (p.25 in part 2)

N Review or update names (See
  DATA NAMES, p.37)

S SEARCH to select particular
  records for display or print,
  e.g., all names beginning with
  B or all birthdays in this
  month or all OUTLET issues
  from No.55 onwards. You can
  search further and add more
  selections to an existing list
  of selections.See SEARCH MODE,
  p.09, Part 2.

I Invert the SELECTed status of
  every record. Selected records
  will become unselected and
  vice versa, e.g., if you had a
  selection of all names start-
  ing with B previously then all
  names NOT starting with B are
  displayed.

R Reset the SELECT status of ALL
  records to UNSELECTED. Nothing
  now displays in DISPLAY MODE
  (screen will show"Sel=00000").
  To re-display the whole file,
  use I to invert.

P Purge(erase) ALL selected rec-
  ords. NOTE THAT IT TAKES SOME
  TIME TO PURGE LARGE FILES!

T Compute total and average of
  numeric data in a chosen field
  for all selected records -also
  available from DISPLAY mode.
  See TOTAL/AVERAGE,p.23,Part 2.

V Save program and file, or file
  only.See LOAD/SAVE,p.25,Part 2

U User-defined BASIC (see p.34 &
  p.35 in Part 2).

           EMPTY FILE
           ----------
Keep one copy of MASTERFILE that
is empty of headings, data names
and report format definitions as
well as pure data, and use it
whenever you need to start a new
file application. The original
program may be used or you could
save its empty file separately
to load as needed. If not,do the
following to empty a file...

1.Erase all records: MM RIPY

2.Erase all report formats:MM E
then R1XY to erase Report Format
1, R2XY to erase 2, and so on.

3.Erase all data names:MM N then
EY EY etc. until no more names
are displayed.

Afterwards you can resave the
whole MASTERFILE program in the
usual way using the following
keys, with for example...

        MM V P "MFEMPTY"

This also provides you with an
extra back-up of the program.
If you (also) wish to save the
empty file by itself use, for
example...
        MM V F "EMPTY.D"

(avoiding the same name as the
main program on the same disc!).

Data files are saved as Spectrum
DATA files in F$.Note that empty
files still contain essential
system information within F$.


           DATA NAMES
           ----------
It's advisable but not essential
to give each data reference a
name, e.g., in OUTDEX,the field
holding the item of data which
is the title has data REFERENCE
"T" and data NAME "TITLE".

Data names can be 1 to 128 char-
acters long,are part of the file
and useful with AUTO-PROMPT. Use
MM N to add,review or alter data
names. The same menu appears as
in ADD A RECORD but options P, D
& = don't work.A adds a new data
name,N browses,R replaces a name
and E erases. M or D returns to
MM. The order in which you add
data names is the order in which
data is auto-prompted.


           EDIT MODE
           ---------
Entered via MM E, EDIT mode is
concerned with the creation and
modification of report formats.
Up to 36 report formats may be
defined,giving that many logical
views of your selected records.
Some effort is required to edit
a report format, but this is
typically a once-only task.

The menu reached via MM E lets
you create a new format via A or
review/alter an existing format
via R.

After A or R, give the report
reference, 0-9, A-Z as prompted.
The report reference "Ref n" is
then shown at top right while in
EDIT mode.

When a report format is first
created, it is given the follow-
ing GENERAL characteristics:

 (a) Background paper colour of
     7 (white)

 (b) Screen border colour of 7

 (c) Sequence: none, unsorted.
     (ie, same order as entered)

 (d) Interval of one record
     every two lines

You can change these at any time
by using menu option R while
GENERAL is displayed. You are
then prompted for (a) to (d).

Reply to (a) and (b) with 0-7.


Answer(c)with the data reference
of the data by which the report
is to be sequenced (order you
want the file displayed), e.g.,
OUTDEX can be listed in order of
Title, Issue or Category. Just
press ENTER for no sequence and
records will be displayed in the
order they were entered (added).

Reply to (d) with 1-22, being
the interval down the screen at
which records are displayed. To
show just one record per screen
enter 22; for one record every
line enter 1.

You then add the REPORT ELEMENTS
which are of two distinct types:
1.fixed headings,boxes,lines,etc
2.actual data fields(references)

Fixed elements are shown on each
displayed page unchanged whereas
data fields in a report format
will display the data item in
that field for each record.

For example, a name and address
file may have a fixed heading at
the top of the page: "NAMES AND
ADDRESSES"in a box or underlined
and it will show on every page.
The fields(data references) you
select to appear in a report
will draw the data from the file
(the actual names and addresses
in the example); this will vary
down the page and from page to
page. You do not have to include
EVERY defined field in every
report. A report might just list
the names without the addresses.

Conversely, You can even display
the same data more than once and
there is no limit to the number
of elements other than space.

Use EDIT menu option A to add a
new element then a new menu asks
what kind of element. Remember,
all elements except data are
fixed and will always appear
whether or not any records data
gets selected. They are:

  L Literal - e.g. title, column
    heading, currency symbol

  B Box - a rectangle drawn to
    pixel resolution

  H Horizontal line

  V Vertical line


For a LITERAL,press L and supply
the data as prompted, i.e. line
number, Micro-print (see p.51),
Column,Paper,Bright 0/1, Inverse
0/1, Flash 0/1 and Literal text.
If text overflows the right-most
column it will resume on the
next line, Column 0. Ink colour
is not prompted as MASTERFILE
always uses contrast.

To obtain a different ink on a
background of white, enter 0 to
3 as the paper colour and invert
it. Similarly,on a background of
black, enter 4 to 7 and invert
it. However, if using Microprint
then make sure the text starts
and ends on a horizontal posit-
ion divisible by 8 (for 51 col)
or 4 (for 42 col) else you may
get inverse marks at each end!

Both the following are for the
Spectrum graphic coordinates 0
to 255 left to right and 0 to
175 bottom to top. If in doubt,
experiment...

For a BOX, press B and supply as
prompted the co-ordinates of the
top left corner, depth in pixels
less 1, width in pixels less 1.

For a LINE, press H or V and
supply as prompted the left-most
or top-most pixel and the length
in pixels less 1.

So much for the static elements
- now we consider the data field
elements. Data elements specify
which items of a record are to
be displayed,where and with what
attributes.

Having pressed A to add an elem-
ent, press D and reply to quite
a long list of prompts (as an
example, the NAMES field of a
name and address file will be
used)...

(a) DATA REFERENCE of the target
item, (e.g.,N if used for NAMES)

(b) LINE:the first line at which
selected records are to start
listing. (e.g., line 2 if line 0
is a header and line 1 is blank)

(c) MICRO-PRINT:see p.51.

(d) COLUMN (e.g., 0 if to start
at left of screen. Maximum is 31
for 32 column mode, 41 for 42
column and 50 for 52 column).


(e) WIDTH - number of columns
wide: MASTERFILE lets you list
data in any character rectangle
(this should be at least as wide
as the longest anticipated name
in our example but can be wider:
It will not waste memory; you
only need to make sure it does
not overlap something else on
the screen. Also, both text and
any blank area within this width
will be nicely coloured in if a
paper colour and PAD is chosen.

(f) DEPTH -number of lines deep.
The same applies as for WIDTH
but DEPTH must not be more than
INTERVAL in the GENERAL section
referred to earlier (you can't
cram say, a six-line record in
every four lines!) but it can be
less.

(g) SPECTRUM ATTRIBUTES - paper,
bright or not, inverse or not,
flash or not.

(h) PAD or not.Pad will fill the
rectangle with the chosen paper
colour

(i) NULL TEXT. If data is absent
in a record, then you can supply
text to appear in its place,
e.g. "not known" or "-": the
default null text is a single
space.In OUTDEX,this feature has
been used to store six category
names as default and then the
UNWANTED categories are "masked"
off with a colon! This saves a
lot of memory but it definitely
was NOT the real purpose of this
ability of MASTERFILE!


Another similar interesting use
of Null Text is to use an unused
data reference in a data
element. This is a way of, for
instance, putting lines of
dashes between records. The null
text is a line of dashes and
always appears because the
target data reference is never
present in the records. Data
elements are put on the screen
in the order they are defined
so, if the position of the text
at either end may vary then this
"dashes" element should be put
in first so that text overlaps
it. To clarify this, study how
the DOTS element has been used
in OUTDEX by looking at both the
report format for say, T and the
display itself. This also works
on the print-out!

Numeric data will be shown right
justified, provided the field
depth is 1 and Pad=N. This means
values will all be listed in the
same tens and units columns etc.

The above fully describes how an
item of the first selected
record appears in your report.
Items from further records will
be displayed lower down the
screen, at whatever interval you
have in GENERAL.

You can browse through report
elements with N (next element).
Any element can be replaced
using R and then following the
prompts. There is also an erase
element option: E. You can go
straight to DISPLAY mode via D
to see the result of changes.

The report format as a whole can
be erased using X and a complete
report format can be copied with
C. This is very useful when you
want to create a format similar
to one already built;perhaps you
just want the same layout but a
different sequence(as in OUTDEX:
title, issue and category).

After C or X you see the initial
EDIT menu.

Plan your report formats on
paper before coding them. Aim
for an exact number of records
per screen, by choosing suitable
line numbers and interval.
Beware overlapping elements, or
overlapping records - MASTERFILE
does not check for these.


          MICRO-PRINT
          -----------
Normal Spectrum character size
is 32 columns across the screen.
By compressing the characters to
5 or 6-bit width instead of the
normal 8, more characters a line
are possible. The Micro-print
feature allows two degrees of
"compression": either 42 or 51
column pitch. Thus any display
can show any mix of normal or
compressed text. Both literal
and data text can be so treated.

The advantages of Micro-print
are not only that more data per
screen is seen but, especially
with 42-pitch,the clarity can be
enhanced due to the improved
character proportions.

The only drawback is that Micro-
print takes a little longer to
display than normal 32-column.

The way to specify Micro-print
is as follows...

In EDIT mode, when supplying a
literal or data element, you are
prompted with "Micro-prt Y/N".
Reply with the N key to stay
with 32-pitch for that element.
Otherwise press Y and you are
prompted with "42-Pitch Y/N".
Reply Y to select 42-pitch, or N
to select 51-pitch characters.
When you prompted for column and
width (data elements), you will
find MASTERFILE lets you extend
to column 41 or 50, according to
the chosen pitch.

FLASH does not operate on Micro
print text. EDIT mode displays
Micro-print pitch in place of
the FLASH status when you review
such elements of a report.

Notice that when giving a column
number for a Micro-print element
the number is in terms of the
selected pitch -NOT the standard
Spectrum 32-column BASIC TAB or
AT positions. The approximate
"real" column number is 6/8 or
5/8 of the Micro-print column.

Because of attribute geometry of
the Spectrum, paper and ink col-
ours must change only at natural
character boundaries so Micro-
print text colour extends both
sides to a natural character
edge.

    CREATING A SPECIAL FIXED
    REFERENCE OR INFO PAGE
    ------------------------
To make a spare, fixed info page
in a file, like the help page in
OUTDEX, define a special report
format. Use LITERAL text for the
fixed text, make it UNSEQUENCED
with an interval of 22 (in the
general characteristics) and add
a dummy data reference (even if
you do not need it)to just print
one blank square anywhere (as
null text - no record actually
includes the dummy).If you don't
there is a delay each time the
page is displayed while the file
is searched.In a large file this
may seem like a long time when
you just want a quick look at a
help page!


        WORD PROCESSING
        ---------------
In DISPLAY mode, MASTERFILE does
rudimentary word-processing so
leading blanks are ignored, a
clean left margin is maintained,
and word-breaks minimised. This
means text can be entered
without having to worry about
spacing. MASTERFILE will start a
new line rather than split a
word (wordwrap), unless the last
line is already reached.

The vertical line character,VLC,
has a special use in MASTERFILE.
A VLC is found using Extended
Mode+Symbol Shift-S. The VLC is
a "start-new-line" signal, so
you may wish to use it in an
address, for example.

Enter text as single data items,
with VLCs as line separators. In
UPDATE mode, item data is shown
without word-processing and any
VLCs are visible(these appear as
a vertical line in the original
character set but as the common
"carriage return" symbol in the
new, thicker character set). In
DISPLAY mode they do not appear.
A VLC acts as a space when text
reaches the paragraph bottom.

If there is insufficient room to
display an item, truncation
occurs on-screen (text is cut
short) but the full data is kept
in the file and will print in
full if you have left room when
formatting your printer spec.
(see Extended printing p.47,Pt2)

       ADD A RECORD MODE
       -----------------
To add a new record, use MM A.
This puts an EMPTY record on the
end of the file. The menu then
lets you add(insert) an item(A),
auto-prompt items (P) or exit to
DISPLAY mode (D) or to MM (M).

IF A BLANK RECORD APPEARS IN THE
FILE YOU PROBABLY CAME TO THIS
MENU (BY ACCIDENT?)AND THEN JUST
EXITED WITHOUT ADDING ANY DATA.

To add a data item to a record,
use A and supply data reference
and text, maximum 128 characters
with trailing spaces dropped. No
tokens, graphics or colour codes
allowed or they are shown as "?"
CAPS SHIFT/LOCK may be used.

An alternative method of data
entry is via P which is Auto-
Prompt. This causes MASTERFILE
to solicit each item by scanning
your data names. Auto-prompt ob-
viates the need to remember all
your data references and makes
it unlikely to omit items. Enter
text, ending with ENTER for each
prompted item.MASTERFILE briefly
displays it before prompting the
next item.If no data for an item
use ENTER on its own.

  ENTER -  QUICKLY FOLLOWED BY
  SPACE, will END THE PROMPTS!

Having added one or more items
you can browse through to check
using N for each next item and
you can replace using R or erase
using E.

Instead of holding N down to get
to an item,summon it direct with
G then a target data reference.
If you attempt to G an item not
present,MASTERFILE waits for you
to give a different reference or
back out via ENTER.

If you use R to to replace and
wish to back out just delete
your input, if any, and press
ENTER. MASTERFILE will leave the
original item intact.

TO ADD ANOTHER RECORD WITHOUT
GOING BACK TO MM, PRESS "=" THEN
A OR P ETC.

To insert a record at a partic-
ular place in a file, see COPY
FILE, p.63 in DISPLAY MODE.

          DISPLAY MODE
          ------------
DISPLAY mode is for viewing sel-
ected records in a way dictated
by your report format (the last
used or first created). You can
display via MM D but other menus
also offer the D option. Another
way to DISPLAY mode is via MM C
(select a report reference).

Contents of lines 0-21 depend on
your report format. Line 22 is..

 Report n    Q=menu     No more
  (red)     (yellow)     (blue)

where n is the report reference,
and the blue legend can be"more"
when there is not enough room on
the screen for all your selected
records.

Once line 22 is displayed - some
sequenced reports can take a few
moments to fill the page -a list
of menu functions is available.
The menu is not normally shown,
but you can summon it with Q -
and banish it again with Q. YOU
CANNOT SELECT FROM THE "Q" MENU
WHILE IT IS STILL DISPLAYED. The
functions are as follows...

N   NEXT PAGE(If "more is shown)

1-9 Advance the report by 1-9
    records. Use 1-9 to position
    a record at top-of-screen
    ready for options U,E,O & C.

0   ZERO. Backspace one record.
    For big, sequenced reports
    it may take many MINUTES if
    near the end so avoid!

B   BEGIN again at the first
    record in the selection.


P   PRINT screen:a simple screen
    COPY [Edit BASIC Line 4010
    to desired syntax if fails.
    (See also alternate Extended
    Printing, p.48 in Part 2).
    Press S for the current page
    and A for the current page
    and all further pages. To
    abort, BREAK and GO TO 1.


U   UPDATE top-most displayed
    record. If DISPLAY mode is
    resumed from UPDATE mode the
    same target record is shown.

E   ERASE top record(Y confirms)


O   (letter)OMIT top-most record
    from current SELECTION. The
    record is NOT erased.

C   COPY the top record. A new
    identical record is inserted
    just after it which can now
    be altered via U etc.Here is
    a way of inserting a record
    at a particular place in the
    file(for unsequenced reports
    displayed in the order you
    entered them). IT'S POSSIBLE
    TO PRESS C WITHOUT NOTICING!
    IF A COPY OF A RECORD SHOULD
    APPEAR THEN YOU KNOW WHY!

S   SEARCH (see p.09, Part 2).

T   TOTAL/AVERAGE calculation
    displayed(see p.23, Part 2).


R   REPORT: Select a different
    report format, RESUMING AT
    THE SAME TOP RECORD AS NOW
    CURRENTLY DISPLAYED.You type
    a new report reference.So,it
    just needs two keys to
    switch from one report to
    another. The reports need
    not be in the same sequence.
    This feature is useful to
    switch from a summary report
    of say, 20 records a page,
    to a full expansion,1 record
    per page, of the top record.

M   MAIN MENU exit.Return to MM.

Q   QUICK MENU (displays THESE
    options!). YOU CANNOT SELECT
    WHILE IT'S DISPLAYED!PRESS Q
    AGAIN BEFORE SELECTING.


          UPDATE MODE
          -----------

This is where the items of a
record can be reviewed, replaced
or erased and new items added.
The target record for update is
always the top one displayed in
DISPLAY mode so to update a
particular record you would
either browse through the file
using N and 0-9 until the record
is at the top of the screen or
use SEARCH MODE.

Options are almost identical to
those described in ADD A RECORD
MODE. Use D to resume DISPLAY
mode at the same target record
on completion of the update.
.

Introduction to MASTERFILE & Changes  by Brian Cavers

```text
   --------------------------
```

MASTERFILE was published in the early days of the Spectrum but I don't know of any other Spectrum all-purpose, record-keeping pro- gram to beat it! The publishers, Campbell Systems, have now made it public domain so it can be freely copied.

MASTERFILE enables you to keep records of almost any type, show them sorted in any order either on screen or printed, either the complete file or a selected part of it and search  the file for a particular item or items, e.g., every London address from a name and address list!

You can add, modify or remove a record and the whole file can be saved to tape or disc for later retrieval or update.

The original was for 48K use and became Version 09 very early on. This worked only with ZX-type printers but Campbell later put out "MFPRINT" which modifies the main MASTERFILE to use full-size printers.

I have seen a Version 10 but I think it was someone's modified version and not an "official" version number. There is also a 128K version for the +3 with an increased storage capacity and extra features which will be in a later (next?) issue on the +3 OUTLET disc only.

In addition, I have made further improvements to the original 48K Version 9 which I have named 9B. This now includes a choice of an extra, thicker, screen character set; the ability to "ADD" or "MERGE" separate files; no need for a "pre-loader" to clear down RAMTOP; the extra MFPRINT of course; as well as lots of extra little goodies I shall describe later.

The foregoing does use a little more of the precious memory even though I have improved memory- saving on the BASIC that already existed so I have also created a "bare-minimum" version that is the original Version 09 with the BASIC reduced even more.

I recommend you use Version 9B. If a file becomes too large you can either split it into two or, if preferred, load it into the cut-down version and add more to it but note that it will not then load into the full version.

Our OUTLET index: OUTDEX which became full up last December, is now to be relaunched each month as a MASTERFILE file. This was the main reason for my writing a "MERGE" routine so that you can add each month's new index data to your main OUTDEX file until it is full, at which point just start a "Volume 2". An advantage of MASTERFILE is that it does not matter which order you add these files as they are shown in the right order.

The full original OUTDEX (Issues 1 to 63) has been converted to MASTERFILE format and is in this issue as "OUTDEX1.63". Just load it in MASTERFILE.

All later months' data up to last month is in a separate file "OUTDX64.74". Future OUTDEX data will usually be one month behind with a filename, eg.,"OUTDEX.75" so just keep adding (merging) them into "OUTDX64.74"and resave as eg, "OUTDEX64.75" until full!

We've TWO parts of instructions so for a fast look at MASTERFILE press N (twice!) and follow the menus to load and display OUTDEX data else read on or print the following more detailed info...

When MASTERFILE was declared in the public domain I appealed for readers to send in copies so an assessment of the different ver- sions could be made etc. So many readers kindly helped out that I am confident we have everything and all instructions.

There were just too many people to credit everyone here but each should have received an individ- ual acknowledgement on return of their disc. THANKS AGAIN TO ALL!

We have received various bits of instructions and programs and it is possible some parts have been published in the SDC Newsletters for which we give credit. I have modified and added also!

As saved in OUTLET, MASTERFILE includes our usual OUTLET 'link' BASIC and title page. All this superfluous programming erases itself automatically when you use the RUN option. DO NOT USE THE MASTERFILE 'SAVE PROGRAM' OPTION TO RESAVE MASTERFILE ON YOUR OUTLET DISC AS "MFILE" OR IT WILL NO LONGER LINK TO OUTLET (in fact it is always best to keep any original program as a back up - completely unchanged in case of disaster!).

In addition, take care when you save a file separately from the main program that you don't use the same name as your program, e.g., "MFILE" or it will over- write the program if it is on the same disc!        - Brian

GLOSSARY OF TERMS

```text
        -----------------
```

ADD: Merge another file into the current file from disc/tape - OR insert a new RECORD in the file.

ARGUMENT: In a SEARCH, something with which RECORDS are compared.

AUTO-PROMPT:Where new data ITEMS are solicited automatically.

BACK OUT: Change one's mind.

COMMAND MODE: In BASIC.

DATA NAME: Fuller name of DATA REFERENCE or FIELD.

DATA REFERENCE: Letter A-Z by which FIELDS are identified.

DISPLAY MODE: Where SELECTED RECORDS are viewed in a REPORT.

EDIT MODE: Where REPORT formats are created or altered.

EMPTY FILE:One devoid of RECORDS DATA NAMES or REPORT FORMATS.

FIELD: Part of record,identified by its DATA REFERENCE,that holds one ITEM of data.

FILE:Whole collection of RECORDS (subdivided into ITEMS)and their associated REPORT FORMATS etc.

GENERAL:Global Report attributes

INVERT: Reverse SELECTED status of all RECORDS - thus UNSELECTED become SELECTEd and vice versa.

ITEM:Data,1-128 characters long, a subsection of a RECORD. One ITEM of data fits into one FIELD of the file identified by its DATA REFERENCE and DATA NAME.

LITERAL TEXT: Fixed text, e.g., a heading in a REPORT.

MAIN MENU: The MENU offered when the program is first run (=MM).

MENU: List of key options.

MICRO-PRINT:Screen text shown at 42 or 51 characters a line.

MM: MAIN MENU.

NULL TEXT: Text displayed in a REPORT in the absence of an ITEM

PAD:Fill out data with spaces in a REPORT.

PROMPT: Instruction to the user, or small MENU.

PURGE:Erase all SELECTED RECORDS

RAM: Random Access Memory avail- able for operating the program

RECORD:Set of upto 26 ITEMS,each with a different DATA REFERENCE.

REPORT:List of SELECTED RECORDS.

REPORT ELEMENT:Part of a REPORT, e.g., heading, box, data spec.

REPORT REFERENCE: Character 0-9 or A-Z identifying a REPORT.

RESET: Clear SELECTED status of all RECORDS, ie, deselect all.

SEARCH MODE: Where RECORDS are SELECTED or otherwise by compar- ing with an ARGUMENT.

SELECTED: Eligible for display in a REPORT.

SEQUENCE:Where RECORDS are shown in order of a chosen FIELD.

UPDATE MODE: Where a RECORD can be altered.

USER BASIC: BASIC which you can supply for special processing.

VLC: Vertical Line Character=New line.see WORDPROCESSING(Page 55)

MASTERFILE INSTRUCTIONS

```text
     -----------------------
```

If any of the terms used are unfamiliar, refer to the  preceding  glossary that starts  on Page 09.

OVERVIEW

```text
            --------
```

MASTERFILE is a filing and re- trieval system for use with any Spectrum. It is almost entirely machine-coded for compactness and speed and offers about 30K of data per file.The program can be saved and loaded with a file "on board" for immediate access or files can be saved and loaded independently (tape or disc).

Because MASTERFILE display form- ats are user-defined, the range of applications is enormous both for domestic use and business. Address lists,library catalogues personnel files, stock inventor- ies, school exam results, family trees - all these are easily handled by MASTERFILE. Some of the main features are:

* Menu-driven, dynamic,variable- length file.

* User-defined data names and report formats.

* File search by any number of criteria.

* Sequence order by any field.

* Display 1-22 records a screen.

* Micro-print feature for up to 51 characters per line.

* Print to any printer including the old ZX-types.

* Total and average calculations for fields containing values.

* Optional User BASIC where the file data is passed to BASIC in sequence so the user can perform any other calculations or modification of the data.

* Update,copy and erase records.

* Save or load files or program.

* Speed of operation.

MASTERFILE FILE STRUCTURE

```text
    -------------------------
```

A file is an organised collect- ion of data (subdivided into records further subdivided into data items) which is stored on cassette or disc and which can be loaded into RAM for enquiry or update purposes.

It may be simple as a telephone list or complex like a personnel data file but, in every case, a file is made up of records, each of which is usually related to a particular identifying item e.g. a person, recipe or part-number.

Each record is in turn made up of up to 26 different items of data e.g., name, address, stock level, telephone number.

Data items are all treated by MASTERFILE as being of variable length (so no memory is wasted) up to 128 characters in length.

There is no rigid record struct- ure and items can be stored in any order within a record as they may always be displayed or printed in the order you define. Each data item in a record is in an individual field identified by its unique data reference letter. A record can have many DIFFERENT fields but cannot have the SAME one more than once (eg, if you wanted both home AND work phone numbers you must have two different fields or put them in together and treat as one item. All data is stored in character format (as text or digits).

One of the many advantages of a computer file over a card index system is that you can sort it into any order. MASTERFILE does not actually sort your file into order (as stored) but instead DISPLAYS it in any chosen sorted order (a much faster method).You can thus have different logical views of the same data in diff- erent sequences as well as your original date-entered order.

Further, you can be selective about which items are required in a report and choose the display style. You may compose a report format for each view of the file you need. Once these formats are built,they are saved automatically as part of a file.

While items are referred to with a single reference letter which denotes its field,you can assoc- iate a full word or phrase with each such reference. MASTERFILE will display these whenever you use data references especially in AUTO-PROMPT (p.58). We call them "DATA NAMES" and these are also stored automatically as part of your file.

PLANNING A FILE

```text
         ---------------
```

We recommend you work through the section entitled EXERCISE on Page 3 of the next part of these instructions before starting your own file. After that, we suggest the following approach..

The most important task is to decide what data is to go into each record. Allocate a letter A-Z to each kind of data you wish to store. Try to estimate an average record size by adding together what you think will be the usual number of characters in each item. Add 1 for each reference letter (which is also stored). Divide this into 30,000 to get the approximate maximum number of records. Also allow a few dozen bytes for EACH report format which you will compose. Is the answer enough? If not,can you reduce anywhere?For example, where the length of a particular item of data is purely optional, e.g., personal notes, you may prefer to keep these brief and thus get more records in a file.

Remember,any item can be present or not in a record. For example, if you define a field for an item of data that is a phone number, you don't need to use that field in any particular record -it can be empty.However, you cannot have more than one item of the SAME data reference in one record. For example: you couldn't enter TWO phone numbers as SEPARATE ITEMS each with the data reference "T" in one record but you may put them both in together as one item. This would not waste space on those records with only one phone number but you must leave room on-screen in case there were two. Otherwise, define a separate field (data reference) as say,"X" for "Xtra" phone number!.

The next step is to allocate a name or description for each data reference. For example, if you have chosen the data refer- ence letter "T" for a telephone number field then you might use "TELEPHONE" as the data name.

This is optional however; you do not need to give a full name at all if you don't want to but it is useful - and almost essential if using AUTO-PROMPT (see p.3 of the next part of these instruct- ions).The method of allocating this name is as described in DATA NAMES (p.37) after creating an EMPTY FILE (p.35).

Next, add just a few records,see ADD A RECORD MODE (p.57).

Next comes the hard work where you must design and specify the way you want to view your file. Remember that you can have many different views, different sequences, different formats and different contents.

Start with a simple format - it may be helpful to plan it on paper first.Leave embellishments such as lines and boxes until last after you have "frozen" the positions of your data and head- ings. Give special attention to the "interval" which affects the spacing between the displayed records - see EDIT MODE (p.38), MICROPRINT (p.51) and WORDPROC- ESSING (p.55).

MENUS, PROMPTS, MODES

```text
     ---------------------
```

MASTERFILE menus are yellow and respond to upper-case or lower- case keys impartially. When MASTERFILE is loaded it presents the Main Menu: MM. The MM screen also displays the file name (up to 10 characters) and the MASTER FILE version number.

When a key corresponding to one of the options is used, MASTER FILE either takes the indicated action, or immediately offers another menu or prompt. A prompt is a one-line instruction or menu in the lower part of the screen, and takes priority over any other menu.

All the yellow menus and prompts respond to just a single key but where MASTERFILE needs a textual response, the flashing L cursor appears and you terminate your response with the ENTER key.

MASTERFILE nearly always offers a menu or prompt but there is one exception: when in DISPLAY mode the menu would obliterate your display, so it is not usually shown. But you can overlay your display with the menu by using the Q key - BUT USE Q AGAIN to REMOVE the menu.

MASTERFILE operates in a variety of modes - usually shown by a blue heading EXCEPT in DISPLAY mode where ALL lines 0-21 are left to you.

DISPLAY mode will always show "Report n" in red on line 22. Important modes are described in the glossary and some modes: MM, SEARCH, DISPLAY - are accessible by several menu routes.

It would be a little dangerous to allow a single-key response to erase data, so MASTERFILE always asks for confirmation via the "Y" key.Likewise, User BASIC is potentially drastic, and again requires Y to confirm. If you see "Y to confirm" you can back out with any key except Y. Version 9B User BASIC exits to an extra menu which includes a further option for "User BASIC processing" which, as provided, simply STOPS.

BASIC COMMAND MODE

```text
       ------------------
```

With a few exceptions,MASTERFILE runs under machine code control and the BREAK key is ineffective but if you need to modify the Basic or add your own User Basic then you must get into COMMAND mode.

This can be done when MASTERFILE offers a flashing L cursor, e.g. press L at MM. If you then press the CURSOR DOWN key, you get "H STOP in INPUT". Alternatively, select the User BASIC menu then BREAK will work. You are now in COMMAND mode and can list and alter the BASIC.

To resume MASTERFILE processing, enter "GO TO 1" which takes you to the Main Menu again. GO TO 1 should also be used to recover any accidental drop into COMMAND mode.Do not CLEAR or RUN because it will crash MASTERFILE and you will lose any data not SAVEd.

GETTING STARTED

```text
         ---------------
```

MASTERFILE uses several linked files...

MFILE  main program MF.C  main code SCRNEDIT.C  screen report editor MFPRINT.C  ext. printer overlay FORMSPEC  formats printer spec ANYNAME  your printer specs. ANYNAME  your data files

In addition there is the cutdown version: MFILE.MIN and MFMIN.C.

You will normally load MFILE and this loads the main code. It can be used immediately without any change but you will normally re- save it as your working copy on another disc using any name you wish for the main program.

When a data file is in memory, it will be saved with the main program so you can name the main program with a name relevant to the file, e.g.,"BIRTHDAYS". When you reload that copy of the pro- gram all the data is immediately available. Alternatively, save the file on its own and load it into the main program when you need it..

MAIN MENU OPTIONS

```text
        -----------------
```

The main menu represents the top logical level of processing and offers functions which affect the file as a whole. Some func- tions are described more fully elsewhere.

A Add a new record to the end of the file. A one-byte record is inserted and you can see the "Recs=" and "Sel=" counts inc- rement. See ADD A RECORD(p.57)

C Lists all report formats (WITH THE FIRST-ENTERED LITERAL TEXT HEADING) of each report which you can select to display the data in that report format.You can use ENTER to return to MM.

D Go directly to DISPLAY mode to view selected records using the last report format used or the first one created if not yet displayed. If there are no report formats yet, EDIT mode is entered.Several other menus offer a D option. See DISPLAY MODE (p.60).

E EDIT mode (p.38) to review or update screen report formats.

OR...

EXTENDED PRINTER options (p.47 of Part 2) [the Main Menu will show the current E option].

L Load a file which has been saved via MM V,F etc. See LOAD AND SAVE (p.25 in part 2)

N Review or update names (See DATA NAMES, p.37)

S SEARCH to select particular records for display or print, e.g., all names beginning with B or all birthdays in this month or all OUTLET issues from No.55 onwards. You can search further and add more selections to an existing list of selections.See SEARCH MODE, p.09, Part 2.

I Invert the SELECTed status of every record. Selected records will become unselected and vice versa, e.g., if you had a selection of all names start- ing with B previously then all names NOT starting with B are displayed.

R Reset the SELECT status of ALL records to UNSELECTED. Nothing now displays in DISPLAY MODE (screen will show"Sel=00000"). To re-display the whole file, use I to invert.

P Purge(erase) ALL selected rec- ords. NOTE THAT IT TAKES SOME TIME TO PURGE LARGE FILES!

T Compute total and average of numeric data in a chosen field for all selected records -also available from DISPLAY mode. See TOTAL/AVERAGE,p.23,Part 2.

V Save program and file, or file only.See LOAD/SAVE,p.25,Part 2

U User-defined BASIC (see p.34 & p.35 in Part 2).

EMPTY FILE

```text
           ----------
```

Keep one copy of MASTERFILE that is empty of headings, data names and report format definitions as well as pure data, and use it whenever you need to start a new file application. The original program may be used or you could save its empty file separately to load as needed. If not,do the following to empty a file...

1.Erase all records: MM RIPY

2.Erase all report formats:MM E then R1XY to erase Report Format 1, R2XY to erase 2, and so on.

3.Erase all data names:MM N then EY EY etc. until no more names are displayed.

Afterwards you can resave the whole MASTERFILE program in the usual way using the following keys, with for example...

MM V P "MFEMPTY"

This also provides you with an extra back-up of the program. If you (also) wish to save the empty file by itself use, for example... MM V F "EMPTY.D"

(avoiding the same name as the main program on the same disc!).

Data files are saved as Spectrum DATA files in F$.Note that empty files still contain essential system information within F$.

DATA NAMES

```text
           ----------
```

It's advisable but not essential to give each data reference a name, e.g., in OUTDEX,the field holding the item of data which is the title has data REFERENCE "T" and data NAME "TITLE".

Data names can be 1 to 128 char- acters long,are part of the file and useful with AUTO-PROMPT. Use MM N to add,review or alter data names. The same menu appears as in ADD A RECORD but options P, D & = don't work.A adds a new data name,N browses,R replaces a name and E erases. M or D returns to MM. The order in which you add data names is the order in which data is auto-prompted.

EDIT MODE

```text
           ---------
```

Entered via MM E, EDIT mode is concerned with the creation and modification of report formats. Up to 36 report formats may be defined,giving that many logical views of your selected records. Some effort is required to edit a report format, but this is typically a once-only task.

The menu reached via MM E lets you create a new format via A or review/alter an existing format via R.

After A or R, give the report reference, 0-9, A-Z as prompted. The report reference "Ref n" is then shown at top right while in EDIT mode.

When a report format is first created, it is given the follow- ing GENERAL characteristics:

(a) Background paper colour of 7 (white)

(b) Screen border colour of 7

(c) Sequence: none, unsorted. (ie, same order as entered)

(d) Interval of one record every two lines

You can change these at any time by using menu option R while GENERAL is displayed. You are then prompted for (a) to (d).

Reply to (a) and (b) with 0-7.

Answer(c)with the data reference of the data by which the report is to be sequenced (order you want the file displayed), e.g., OUTDEX can be listed in order of Title, Issue or Category. Just press ENTER for no sequence and records will be displayed in the order they were entered (added).

Reply to (d) with 1-22, being the interval down the screen at which records are displayed. To show just one record per screen enter 22; for one record every line enter 1.

You then add the REPORT ELEMENTS which are of two distinct types: 1.fixed headings,boxes,lines,etc 2.actual data fields(references)

Fixed elements are shown on each displayed page unchanged whereas data fields in a report format will display the data item in that field for each record.

For example, a name and address file may have a fixed heading at the top of the page: "NAMES AND ADDRESSES"in a box or underlined and it will show on every page. The fields(data references) you select to appear in a report will draw the data from the file (the actual names and addresses in the example); this will vary down the page and from page to page. You do not have to include EVERY defined field in every report. A report might just list the names without the addresses.

Conversely, You can even display the same data more than once and there is no limit to the number of elements other than space.

Use EDIT menu option A to add a new element then a new menu asks what kind of element. Remember, all elements except data are fixed and will always appear whether or not any records data gets selected. They are:

L Literal - e.g. title, column heading, currency symbol

B Box - a rectangle drawn to pixel resolution

H Horizontal line

V Vertical line

For a LITERAL,press L and supply the data as prompted, i.e. line number, Micro-print (see p.51), Column,Paper,Bright 0/1, Inverse 0/1, Flash 0/1 and Literal text. If text overflows the right-most column it will resume on the next line, Column 0. Ink colour is not prompted as MASTERFILE always uses contrast.

To obtain a different ink on a background of white, enter 0 to 3 as the paper colour and invert it. Similarly,on a background of black, enter 4 to 7 and invert it. However, if using Microprint then make sure the text starts and ends on a horizontal posit- ion divisible by 8 (for 51 col) or 4 (for 42 col) else you may get inverse marks at each end!

Both the following are for the Spectrum graphic coordinates 0 to 255 left to right and 0 to 175 bottom to top. If in doubt, experiment...

For a BOX, press B and supply as prompted the co-ordinates of the top left corner, depth in pixels less 1, width in pixels less 1.

For a LINE, press H or V and supply as prompted the left-most or top-most pixel and the length in pixels less 1.

So much for the static elements - now we consider the data field elements. Data elements specify which items of a record are to be displayed,where and with what attributes.

Having pressed A to add an elem- ent, press D and reply to quite a long list of prompts (as an example, the NAMES field of a name and address file will be used)...

(a) DATA REFERENCE of the target item, (e.g.,N if used for NAMES)

(b) LINE:the first line at which selected records are to start listing. (e.g., line 2 if line 0 is a header and line 1 is blank)

(c) MICRO-PRINT:see p.51.

(d) COLUMN (e.g., 0 if to start at left of screen. Maximum is 31 for 32 column mode, 41 for 42 column and 50 for 52 column).

(e) WIDTH - number of columns wide: MASTERFILE lets you list data in any character rectangle (this should be at least as wide as the longest anticipated name in our example but can be wider: It will not waste memory; you only need to make sure it does not overlap something else on the screen. Also, both text and any blank area within this width will be nicely coloured in if a paper colour and PAD is chosen.

(f) DEPTH -number of lines deep. The same applies as for WIDTH but DEPTH must not be more than INTERVAL in the GENERAL section referred to earlier (you can't cram say, a six-line record in every four lines!) but it can be less.

(g) SPECTRUM ATTRIBUTES - paper, bright or not, inverse or not, flash or not.

(h) PAD or not.Pad will fill the rectangle with the chosen paper colour

(i) NULL TEXT. If data is absent in a record, then you can supply text to appear in its place, e.g. "not known" or "-": the default null text is a single space.In OUTDEX,this feature has been used to store six category names as default and then the UNWANTED categories are "masked" off with a colon! This saves a lot of memory but it definitely was NOT the real purpose of this ability of MASTERFILE!

Another similar interesting use of Null Text is to use an unused data reference in a data element. This is a way of, for instance, putting lines of dashes between records. The null text is a line of dashes and always appears because the target data reference is never present in the records. Data elements are put on the screen in the order they are defined so, if the position of the text at either end may vary then this "dashes" element should be put in first so that text overlaps it. To clarify this, study how the DOTS element has been used in OUTDEX by looking at both the report format for say, T and the display itself. This also works on the print-out!

Numeric data will be shown right justified, provided the field depth is 1 and Pad=N. This means values will all be listed in the same tens and units columns etc.

The above fully describes how an item of the first selected record appears in your report. Items from further records will be displayed lower down the screen, at whatever interval you have in GENERAL.

You can browse through report elements with N (next element). Any element can be replaced using R and then following the prompts. There is also an erase element option: E. You can go straight to DISPLAY mode via D to see the result of changes.

The report format as a whole can be erased using X and a complete report format can be copied with C. This is very useful when you want to create a format similar to one already built;perhaps you just want the same layout but a different sequence(as in OUTDEX: title, issue and category).

After C or X you see the initial EDIT menu.

Plan your report formats on paper before coding them. Aim for an exact number of records per screen, by choosing suitable line numbers and interval. Beware overlapping elements, or overlapping records - MASTERFILE does not check for these.

MICRO-PRINT

```text
          -----------
```

Normal Spectrum character size is 32 columns across the screen. By compressing the characters to 5 or 6-bit width instead of the normal 8, more characters a line are possible. The Micro-print feature allows two degrees of "compression": either 42 or 51 column pitch. Thus any display can show any mix of normal or compressed text. Both literal and data text can be so treated.

The advantages of Micro-print are not only that more data per screen is seen but, especially with 42-pitch,the clarity can be enhanced due to the improved character proportions.

The only drawback is that Micro- print takes a little longer to display than normal 32-column.

The way to specify Micro-print is as follows...

In EDIT mode, when supplying a literal or data element, you are prompted with "Micro-prt Y/N". Reply with the N key to stay with 32-pitch for that element. Otherwise press Y and you are prompted with "42-Pitch Y/N". Reply Y to select 42-pitch, or N to select 51-pitch characters. When you prompted for column and width (data elements), you will find MASTERFILE lets you extend to column 41 or 50, according to the chosen pitch.

FLASH does not operate on Micro print text. EDIT mode displays Micro-print pitch in place of the FLASH status when you review such elements of a report.

Notice that when giving a column number for a Micro-print element the number is in terms of the selected pitch -NOT the standard Spectrum 32-column BASIC TAB or AT positions. The approximate "real" column number is 6/8 or 5/8 of the Micro-print column.

Because of attribute geometry of the Spectrum, paper and ink col- ours must change only at natural character boundaries so Micro- print text colour extends both sides to a natural character edge.

CREATING A SPECIAL FIXED REFERENCE OR INFO PAGE

```text
    ------------------------
```

To make a spare, fixed info page in a file, like the help page in OUTDEX, define a special report format. Use LITERAL text for the fixed text, make it UNSEQUENCED with an interval of 22 (in the general characteristics) and add a dummy data reference (even if you do not need it)to just print one blank square anywhere (as null text - no record actually includes the dummy).If you don't there is a delay each time the page is displayed while the file is searched.In a large file this may seem like a long time when you just want a quick look at a help page!

WORD PROCESSING

```text
        ---------------
```

In DISPLAY mode, MASTERFILE does rudimentary word-processing so leading blanks are ignored, a clean left margin is maintained, and word-breaks minimised. This means text can be entered without having to worry about spacing. MASTERFILE will start a new line rather than split a word (wordwrap), unless the last line is already reached.

The vertical line character,VLC, has a special use in MASTERFILE. A VLC is found using Extended Mode+Symbol Shift-S. The VLC is a "start-new-line" signal, so you may wish to use it in an address, for example.

Enter text as single data items, with VLCs as line separators. In UPDATE mode, item data is shown without word-processing and any VLCs are visible(these appear as a vertical line in the original character set but as the common "carriage return" symbol in the new, thicker character set). In DISPLAY mode they do not appear. A VLC acts as a space when text reaches the paragraph bottom.

If there is insufficient room to display an item, truncation occurs on-screen (text is cut short) but the full data is kept in the file and will print in full if you have left room when formatting your printer spec. (see Extended printing p.47,Pt2)

ADD A RECORD MODE

```text
       -----------------
```

To add a new record, use MM A. This puts an EMPTY record on the end of the file. The menu then lets you add(insert) an item(A), auto-prompt items (P) or exit to DISPLAY mode (D) or to MM (M).

IF A BLANK RECORD APPEARS IN THE FILE YOU PROBABLY CAME TO THIS MENU (BY ACCIDENT?)AND THEN JUST EXITED WITHOUT ADDING ANY DATA.

To add a data item to a record, use A and supply data reference and text, maximum 128 characters with trailing spaces dropped. No tokens, graphics or colour codes allowed or they are shown as "?" CAPS SHIFT/LOCK may be used.

An alternative method of data entry is via P which is Auto- Prompt. This causes MASTERFILE to solicit each item by scanning your data names. Auto-prompt ob- viates the need to remember all your data references and makes it unlikely to omit items. Enter text, ending with ENTER for each prompted item.MASTERFILE briefly displays it before prompting the next item.If no data for an item use ENTER on its own.

ENTER -  QUICKLY FOLLOWED BY SPACE, will END THE PROMPTS!

Having added one or more items you can browse through to check using N for each next item and you can replace using R or erase using E.

Instead of holding N down to get to an item,summon it direct with G then a target data reference. If you attempt to G an item not present,MASTERFILE waits for you to give a different reference or back out via ENTER.

If you use R to to replace and wish to back out just delete your input, if any, and press ENTER. MASTERFILE will leave the original item intact.

TO ADD ANOTHER RECORD WITHOUT GOING BACK TO MM, PRESS "=" THEN A OR P ETC.

To insert a record at a partic- ular place in a file, see COPY FILE, p.63 in DISPLAY MODE.

DISPLAY MODE

```text
          ------------
```

DISPLAY mode is for viewing sel- ected records in a way dictated by your report format (the last used or first created). You can display via MM D but other menus also offer the D option. Another way to DISPLAY mode is via MM C (select a report reference).

Contents of lines 0-21 depend on your report format. Line 22 is..

Report n    Q=menu     No more (red)     (yellow)     (blue)

where n is the report reference, and the blue legend can be"more" when there is not enough room on the screen for all your selected records.

Once line 22 is displayed - some sequenced reports can take a few moments to fill the page -a list of menu functions is available. The menu is not normally shown, but you can summon it with Q - and banish it again with Q. YOU CANNOT SELECT FROM THE "Q" MENU WHILE IT IS STILL DISPLAYED. The functions are as follows...

N   NEXT PAGE(If "more is shown)

1-9 Advance the report by 1-9 records. Use 1-9 to position a record at top-of-screen ready for options U,E,O & C.

0   ZERO. Backspace one record. For big, sequenced reports it may take many MINUTES if near the end so avoid!

B   BEGIN again at the first record in the selection.

P   PRINT screen:a simple screen COPY [Edit BASIC Line 4010 to desired syntax if fails. (See also alternate Extended Printing, p.48 in Part 2). Press S for the current page and A for the current page and all further pages. To abort, BREAK and GO TO 1.

U   UPDATE top-most displayed record. If DISPLAY mode is resumed from UPDATE mode the same target record is shown.

E   ERASE top record(Y confirms)

O   (letter)OMIT top-most record from current SELECTION. The record is NOT erased.

C   COPY the top record. A new identical record is inserted just after it which can now be altered via U etc.Here is a way of inserting a record at a particular place in the file(for unsequenced reports displayed in the order you entered them). IT'S POSSIBLE TO PRESS C WITHOUT NOTICING! IF A COPY OF A RECORD SHOULD APPEAR THEN YOU KNOW WHY!

S   SEARCH (see p.09, Part 2).

T   TOTAL/AVERAGE calculation displayed(see p.23, Part 2).

R   REPORT: Select a different report format, RESUMING AT THE SAME TOP RECORD AS NOW CURRENTLY DISPLAYED.You type a new report reference.So,it just needs two keys to switch from one report to another. The reports need not be in the same sequence. This feature is useful to switch from a summary report of say, 20 records a page, to a full expansion,1 record per page, of the top record.

M   MAIN MENU exit.Return to MM.

Q   QUICK MENU (displays THESE options!). YOU CANNOT SELECT WHILE IT'S DISPLAYED!PRESS Q AGAIN BEFORE SELECTING.

UPDATE MODE

```text
          -----------
```

This is where the items of a record can be reviewed, replaced or erased and new items added. The target record for update is always the top one displayed in DISPLAY mode so to update a particular record you would either browse through the file using N and 0-9 until the record is at the top of the screen or use SEARCH MODE.

Options are almost identical to those described in ADD A RECORD MODE. Use D to resume DISPLAY mode at the same target record on completion of the update. .

### Введение в MASTERFILE и доработки Brian Cavers

MASTERFILE появился на свет на заре эпохи Spectrum, но я не знаю ни одной другой универсальной программы ведения баз данных для Спектрума, способной превзойти её! Издатели, Campbell Systems, перевели её в разряд public domain, так что теперь её можно свободно копировать.

MASTERFILE позволяет вести учет практически любых данных, выводить их отсортированными в любом порядке на экран или на печать (как всю базу целиком, так и выбранную её часть), а также производить поиск по определенным элементам — например, найти все лондонские адреса из списка контактов!

Вы можете добавлять, изменять или удалять записи, а всю базу данных целиком можно сохранять на ленту или диск для последующего извлечения или обновления.

Оригинал был рассчитан на 48K и очень быстро эволюционировал до Version 09. Эта версия работала только с ZX-принтерами, однако позже Campbell выпустили утилиту «MFPRINT», модифицирующую основной MASTERFILE для работы с полноразмерными принтерами.

Я встречал Version 10, но, сдается мне, это чья-то самодельная модификация, а не «официальный» релиз. Существует также 128K-версия для +3 с увеличенным объемом хранимых данных и дополнительными возможностями, которая появится в более позднем (следующем?) выпуске OUTLET эксклюзивно на диске для +3.

Кроме того, я внес ряд улучшений в оригинальную 48K Version 9, назвав новую версию 9B. Теперь она включает в себя: выбор дополнительного, более жирного экранного шрифта; возможность объединения («ADD» или «MERGE») отдельных файлов; избавление от предзагрузчика (pre-loader) для сброса RAMTOP; разумеется, встроенный модуль MFPRINT; а также множество других приятных мелочей, о которых я расскажу позже.

Вышеперечисленное отъедает чуть больше драгоценной памяти (хотя я и оптимизировал существовавший бейсик-код для ее экономии), поэтому я также подготовил версию «bare-minimum» — это оригинальная Version 09, в которой BASIC урезан до самого необходимого минимума.

Я рекомендую использовать Version 9B. Если файл станет слишком большим, вы можете либо разбить его на два, либо загрузить в урезанную версию и продолжать вносить данные (но учтите, что после этого он не загрузится в полную версию).

Наш указатель OUTLET — OUTDEX — переполнился в декабре прошлого года и теперь будет перезапущен и станет выходить ежемесячно в виде файла MASTERFILE. Это и было главной причиной написания процедуры «MERGE»: теперь вы можете каждый месяц добавлять новые индексные данные в свой основной файл OUTDEX, пока он не заполнится до предела, после чего просто завести «Том 2». Огромный плюс MASTERFILE в том, что совершенно не важно, в каком порядке вы добавляете эти файлы — они всегда отображаются в правильной последовательности.

Полный оригинальный OUTDEX (выпуски с 1 по 63) был сконвертирован в формат MASTERFILE и представлен в этом номере под именем «OUTDEX1.63». Просто загрузите его в MASTERFILE.

Все последующие данные вплоть до прошлого месяца собраны в отдельном файле «OUTDX64.74». В будущем данные OUTDEX будут обычно отставать на один месяц и называться, к примеру, «OUTDEX.75». Так что просто продолжайте добавлять (сливать) их с «OUTDX64.74» и пересохранять под новыми именами, например «OUTDEX64.75», пока не кончится место!

Инструкция состоит из ДВУХ частей. Если вам не терпится сразу взглянуть на MASTERFILE, нажмите N (дважды!) и следуйте подсказкам меню, чтобы загрузить и посмотреть данные OUTDEX. В противном случае читайте дальше или распечатайте более подробное руководство ниже...

Когда MASTERFILE объявили достоянием общественности, я попросил читателей присылать копии, чтобы оценить различные версии. Откликнулось столько народу, что я уверен: у нас теперь есть вообще всё, включая полную документацию.

Людей пришло слишком много, чтобы перечислять всех поименно, но каждый должен был получить персональную благодарность при возврате диска. ЕЩЕ РАЗ ВСЕМ СПАСИБО!

К нам поступило множество отрывков документации и программ; вполне возможно, что часть этих материалов ранее публиковалась в SDC Newsletters, чему мы отдаем должное. Кое-что я изменил и дополнил сам!

В дистрибутиве OUTLET программа MASTERFILE снабжена нашим стандартным связующим бейсик-модулем ('link') и титульным экраном. Весь этот лишний код автоматически стирается при запуске опции RUN. НЕ ИСПОЛЬЗУЙТЕ В MASTERFILE ОПЦИЮ «SAVE PROGRAM» ДЛЯ ПЕРЕСОХРАНЕНИЯ ПРОГРАММЫ НА ДИСК OUTLET ПОД ИМЕНЕМ «MFILE», ИНАЧЕ ОНА ПЕРЕСТАНЕТ БЫТЬ СВЯЗАНА С МЕНЮ OUTLET (вообще, всегда разумно держать оригинальную программу нетронутой в качестве резервной копии — на случай катастрофы!).

Кроме того, будьте осторожны при отдельном сохранении файлов данных: не давайте им имя основной программы (например, «MFILE»), иначе вы перезапишете саму программу, если сохраняете на тот же диск! — Brian
